hook.firstFrame: A male character pointing at a government building under text BILLIONAIRE TAX EASY MONEY?
hook.firstLine: You think taxing billionaires is easy money? It isn't.

shots.picture: Character standing next to a government building and shares stack under text BILLIONAIRE TAX EASY MONEY?
California ballot proposal box listing 200 plus billionaires and 5 percent net worth tax stamp.
Stack of share certificates representing 100 billion dollars next to a 5 billion dollar tax bill.
Character gesturing toward a wealthy elderly man under title JUST PAY IT?
Locked stack of company shares beside cash safe and declining stock chart visual.
Moving truck carrying Google founders sign driving across California border line.
Character beside voting box rejecting 5 billion bill card under prompt STILL EASY MONEY?

lines.gist: Questions whether taxing wealth is as simple as it seems.
Explains California targeted over 200 billionaires for net worth tax.
Illustrates how a 100 billion fortune creates 5 billion tax.
Asks why the wealthy cannot simply pay cash immediately.
Shows wealth is tied up in stock requiring sales or loans.
Notes billionaire residents moved out of state to avoid tax.
Shows voters rejected measure and repeats the easy money premise.

ending.lastFrame: Male vector character next to vote machine screen with STILL EASY MONEY text overlay.

whyItWorks: Uses simple vector graphics and concrete numbers to make policy debates clear.
Breaks down complex economic concepts like share illiquidity into simple visuals.
Ends with a thematic loop back to the opening question for rewatchability.
